SMTO-SKL-0083 — SMTO's Microsoft 365 request was incomplete or not accepted

GUID: ce41fc28-5442-50df-8d73-d6538e14328e
Slug: microsoft365-invalid-request
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The details SMTO prepared for Microsoft were missing something or weren't accepted, such as an email with no recipient. The request was stopped or refused, so nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were sending an email, give at least one recipient in To, and check that each email address is typed correctly. Microsoft can't send an email with no recipient or a badly formed address.
  2. Name exactly which email, event, contact or file you mean, for example by its subject, date or file name. SMTO needs a clear target so it doesn't send Microsoft a broken or empty reference.
  3. If you were deleting a calendar, choose one you created, not your main calendar. SMTO doesn't allow deleting your main Outlook calendar.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request and the result appears in Outlook, OneDrive or SharePoint.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the request you typed, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve a send or change if the details SMTO shows you look wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 request was rejected as invalid: arguments failed the tool schema or used a '.'/'..' ID, mail_send had no 'to' recipients, the operation was unsupported or targeted the default calendar for deletion, or Microsoft Graph returned 400 Bad Request.

What this means

  • Arguments fail the tool schema, mail_send has no recipients, operation routing is unsupported, or Graph returns HTTP 400. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Arguments fail the tool schema, mail_send has no recipients, operation routing is unsupported, or Graph returns HTTP 400.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish local validation from provider rejection and inspect the specific field or operation.

How to fix it

  • Correct the arguments against the microsoft365 tool schema: supply 'to' for mail_send, use exact IDs returned by earlier reads (never '.' or '..'), and do not attempt calendar_delete on the default calendar. For a Graph 400, compare the request fields with the operation's documented constraints and keep the same account_ref and resource IDs.
  • Correct the identified request fields using the tool schema and provider response; keep exact intended resource identities.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Correct deliberate arguments pass both local schema and provider constraints.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
